From: Devin Howard <devin@acmecorp.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data retention exception request — AcmeCorp

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo today — good discussion. One of the questions that came up with our security and compliance team is whether Redwood can support a 0-retention profile for requests that contain PII. In particular: 

- Can logs be disabled entirely for specific endpoints or API keys?
- If complete disabling is not possible on hosted plans, can we get a shortened retention window (e.g., 0–24 hours) or per-customer custom schedule?
- Are there options for token redaction or not storing KV cache for particular workloads?

Our compliance team would like to see a written exception request/statement and any technical controls you can provide. I attached the Acme data handling requirements doc for reference.

We have a target go-live in November, so we need an answer and proposed approach within two weeks if possible.

Appreciate it —
Devin Howard
Senior Product Manager, AcmeCorp
Devin.Howard@acmecorp.com
Attachments: Acme_Data_Retention_Request.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request — AcmeCorp

Hi Devin — great to chat today.

Short summary / next steps from our side:

1) Quick answers: on Redwood Hosted we don’t offer a built-in 0-retention product by default today for all customers; we can offer shortened retention windows (24–72 hours) and token-level redaction for certain endpoints. For Dedicated or Private deployments, we can support a 0-retention configuration (no logs persisted) with appropriate configuration.

2) Technical follow-up: I’m looping in Rafael (security/infra) to confirm exact controls and any engineering lead times.

3) Legal/DPA: I’m also looping in Marissa for the DPA amendment and any redline language for retention schedules.

4) Ask from you: can you confirm which API paths will carry PII, approximate RPS during peak, and whether you require Redwoods support logs for troubleshooting? That will inform whether we can meet 0-retention on hosted or recommend Dedicated.

Proposed timeline: Rafael to provide an architecture/options summary by EOD 10/02; Marissa to propose DPA language by 10/03; follow-up sync next week to finalize. If that works I’ll set a 30-minute slot.

I attached our retention policy doc for context.

Best,
Camila Reyes

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Devin Howard <devin@acmecorp.com>, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request — AcmeCorp

Hi Devin/Camila —

Technical feasibility notes from infra/security:

- Hosted: default logs (request/response traces and minimal metadata) are retained for 30 days for telemetry and abuse detection. We can offer shortened retention (24–72 hours) and a redaction pipeline that strips or hashes tokens before they are stored. Full 0-retention on our multi-tenant hosted control plane is not available as a self-serve option today due to auditing and abuse-detection constraints.

- Dedicated/Private: for Dedicated instances we can configure the cluster to avoid persisting request/response logs, disable KV cache persistence, and route operational logs to a customer-controlled S3 with lifecycle rules. That configuration can meet a 0-retention objective for user content.

- Engineering/time/cost: enabling on-hosted redaction pipelines and per-API-key retention windows is feasible but will require a scoped change (estimated 3–6 weeks with product and infra prioritization). Dedicated configuration is quicker (1–2 weeks for provisioning + config).

- Support notes: we will need an agreed troubleshooting policy — if logs are disabled, we can provide ephemeral debug sessions (time-boxed) or request sample payloads from Acme with explicit consent.

Next steps I propose:
1) Devin, please confirm the endpoints and whether real-time troubleshooting access is required.
2) If you want 0-retention and are open to Dedicated, we can scope capacity and pricing.
3) If you prefer Hosted, we can scope per-customer retention redaction work (engineering estimate above).

See attached for a short overview of logging controls.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Attachments: Logging_Controls_Overview.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-10-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request — AcmeCorp

Hi all —

From a legal/DPA perspective we can support a bespoke retention schedule via an addendum to the DPA. Key points I would expect to include in the redline: 

- "0-retention" clause limited to specific API keys/endpoints and defined data categories (e.g., PII as defined by Acme).
- Auditability: Redwood will provide configuration evidence and periodic attestations that the retention setting is enabled.
- Support & incident handling: exception process for turning on ephemeral logs for troubleshooting; all such access must be documented and time-boxed.
- Residual metadata: define which metadata (if any) Redwood may retain for operational/security purposes and for how long.

I’ve prepared an initial redline to the DPA for your review (attached). If Acme’s counsel is okay with the language, we can execute via DocuSign and then Rafael can sign off on the technical config.

One ask: Acme legal (Priya) — can you confirm if you will accept an attestation and configuration evidence, or do you require ongoing audit access?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
